title: 'Flock Flocked up'

reading.body:
This is a case of an automated alert being treated as established fact. A camera system flagged a plate as stolen, and the alert was wrong. The stop, the drawn guns, the arrest and the K-9 release all followed from that single false signal, which means the failure sits at the front of the chain rather than in any one officer's decision later on.

The mismatch was present in the alert itself. The image matched a Chevy Malibu, but the alert attached to a red Dodge Ram pickup. Catching it would have taken a human comparing the plate read against the vehicle in front of them before acting, and the facts indicate no such check happened before the stop. Officers only learned the plate was not stolen afterward, when one called it a misread.

What is not established is fault. A Toledo Police Department investigation found no wrongdoing in the use of the K-9, charges were dropped according to the driver's lawyer, and the report that multiple officers are under investigation is a report rather than a finding. Nothing in the facts establishes intent by the officers or by whoever deployed the camera system.

reports.title: Body cam of TPD officers releasing K-9 on man during traffic stop
Man speaks out after police release K-9 on him during traffic stop: 'Traumatized'
TPD investigation finds no wrongdoing in use of K-9 on man during traffic stop
Charges dropped against man Toledo Police released K-9 on during traffic stop, lawyer says

summary:
Toledo police released body camera video Monday showing a traffic stop where an officer released a K-9 on a driver. A FLOCK camera alert said a plate was stolen, but the alert was wrong. The image matched a Chevy Malibu, yet it appeared on a red Dodge Ram pickup. Officers stopped the truck as it left a carryout, drew guns, and ordered driver Brandon Upchurch out. He got out with his hands up, asked why he was stopped, then walked into the grass. The K-9 handler moved closer and the dog was released. Upchurch was arrested and charged with resisting arrest and obstruction.

Officers later learned the plate was not stolen, and one called it a misread. Upchurch received medical attention at the scene. Police said they thought he might flee and did not know if he or a passenger had weapons. The article says multiple Toledo Police Department officers are under investigation. It also says TPD's K-9 policy requires handlers to consider the crime's severity, immediate threats, and whether a suspect is resisting or trying to evade arrest.
